title: Largest Submatrix With Rearrangements
summary: Given a binary matrix of size m × n, you are allowed to rearrange its columns in any order to maximize the area of a submatrix where all elements are 1.
statement: Given a binary matrix of size m × n, you are allowed to rearrange its columns in any order to maximize the area of a submatrix where all elements are 1. Determine the largest possible area of such a submatrix after optimally reordering the columns.
constraints: The binary matrix is rectangular; within each row you may rearrange columns independently.
Return the largest all-ones submatrix area obtainable after rearrangements.
hints: For a fixed bottom row, each column contributes its consecutive-one height; rearrangement lets any widths be grouped.
Update vertical heights, sort them descending, and test height times prefix width.
For each row compute heights, then maximize sorted_heights[width-1]*width.
For each width the largest possible minimum height uses the width tallest columns, and every rectangle has some bottom row.
editorial: For each width the largest possible minimum height uses the width tallest columns, and every rectangle has some bottom row.

tests.explanation: At the final row, two column heights are two, giving area four.
Three height-one columns can be grouped for area three.
